question_frame: Target-mechanism question: through 2024-12-31, how did human genetic evidence establish the relationship between leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 and Parkinson disease; which pathogenic, risk-modifying, and protective variants are supported across ancestries and disease forms; how do altered kinase, GTPase, and related biochemical activities affect validated physiological substrates and downstream phenotypes; and what null, conflicting, incomplete-penetrance, model-specific, replication, correction, or safety evidence limits causal strength or generality? Search PubMed from database inception without language restriction for pedigrees, sequencing and association studies, functional genetics, enzymology, structural biology, phosphoproteomics, cellular studies, animal models, human tissues and biofluids, and evidence syntheses used for reference genealogy. Include human and nonhuman organisms while labeling the evidentiary bridge to human Parkinson disease. Outcomes include segregation, association, penetrance, ancestry dependence, enzyme activity, substrate phosphorylation, cellular trafficking and lysosomal/autophagic phenotypes, neurodegeneration, biomarkers, and clinical relevance.

queries.purpose: Capture recent genetic, mechanistic, substrate, and limiting evidence through the as-of date, then reconcile online-first, issue, correction, and retraction dates during screening.

inclusion_criteria: Include peer-reviewed records indexed in PubMed by the as-of date that directly address LRRK2/PARK8 genetics, variant effects, enzymatic mechanism, physiological substrates, downstream disease-relevant biology, or limitations on those claims.

Include primary human evidence on linkage, segregation, sequencing, association, penetrance, ancestry, pathology, patient-derived materials, tissues, or biofluids; retain reviews and meta-analyses for synthesis context and reference genealogy while tracing decisive claims to primary studies.

Include biochemical, structural, phosphoproteomic, cellular, and animal evidence when it tests LRRK2 activity, variant effects, substrate phosphorylation, or disease-relevant phenotypes; label organism, model, perturbation, and distance from human Parkinson disease.

Include null, negative, conflicting, replication, correction, retraction, loss-of-function, incomplete-penetrance, ancestry-heterogeneity, and toxicity evidence capable of limiting causal strength or generality.
Apply no language exclusion; use translated metadata or accessible abstracts where possible and flag records requiring translation or unavailable full text.

Deduplicate at the canonical PMID level, reconcile DOI and online-first versus issue versions, preserve every query-to-record occurrence link, retain correction and retraction relationships, and fail closed for unresolved conflicting bibliographic identities.

Escalate uncertain variant nomenclature, substrate-versus-downstream-effector classification, conflicting duplicate identity, and claims supported only by inaccessible full text for manual adjudication before synthesis.
exclusion_criteria: Exclude records that mention LRRK2 or Parkinson disease only incidentally and provide no extractable genetic, mechanistic, substrate, disease-bridge, or limiting evidence.
Exclude purely computational predictions, docking studies, or pathway speculation lacking experimental or human genetic validation, except when explicitly labeled as hypothesis-generating context.
Exclude studies focused exclusively on LRRK1 or unrelated kinases unless they provide a direct comparator needed to interpret LRRK2 specificity.
Exclude therapeutic efficacy reports with no information relevant to target engagement, kinase or substrate biology, mechanism, safety limitations, or translation to the proposed causal chain.
Exclude duplicate citations after canonicalization while preserving their query occurrences, alternate publication dates, and links to corrections, errata, or retractions.
Exclude evidence first published after 2024-12-31; record post-cutoff corrections discovered during integrity reconciliation as a temporal coverage gap rather than silently incorporating them.
stop_rules: Execute all twelve planned PubMed query events or stop earlier only for an unrecoverable source failure, recording any budget exhaustion or failed event.

Require sentinel recovery of the PARK8 linkage and independent LRRK2 mutation-discovery anchors plus at least one endogenous Rab-substrate anchor; if missing, pilot spelling, author, historical-name, and substrate-alias expansions within the twelve-event budget before screening.
Stop alias expansion when every concept block has produced relevant records or documented zero yield and the known genetic and substrate anchors are recovered.
Stop expansion after two consecutive expansion events add no new decision-relevant genetic claim, variant, physiological substrate, mechanistic link, limiting result, or primary anchor.
Stop when the twelve-query maximum is reached even if saturation is incomplete, and report unresolved themes and source limitations in coverage gaps.

Consider the search decision-saturated only when additional retrieval is unlikely to change conclusions about genetic causality, variant heterogeneity, enzymatic directionality, physiological-substrate status, or generality limits.
Do not use aggressive NOT clauses; any later exclusion filter must first demonstrate preservation of all recovered anchors.

Keep genetics, enzymatic mechanism, substrate validation, disease-bridge, and challenge evidence separable during screening so a strong result in one branch cannot substitute for missing evidence in another.
coverage_gaps: Only PubMed is available; native forward/backward citation-graph traversal and DOI-metadata expansion are unavailable, so author- and review-linked PubMed queries provide an incomplete proxy.

Dedicated GWAS catalogs, ClinVar or locus-specific variant databases, population reference datasets, and genealogy databases are unavailable; ancestry frequencies, clinical assertions, and penetrance estimates must be derived from PubMed-indexed reports.
Trial registries and regulator sources are unavailable, limiting systematic verification of inhibitor trials, target-engagement status, organ toxicity, and regulatory safety conclusions.
Preprint servers are unavailable, so recent unreviewed findings through 2024-12-31 may be missed.
Patents and chemistry databases are unavailable; medicinal-chemistry prior art and compound-level selectivity are outside the retrievable scope.
PubMed publication-date filtering can imperfectly represent online-first, issue, indexing, correction, and retraction timing; temporal discrepancies require manual reconciliation.
Non-indexed literature, conference proceedings, theses, non-English records without usable translated metadata, and inaccessible full texts may leave residual evidence gaps.
